system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for the Wattlebridge Holdings deal team. Privileged and confidential.**

## Overview

The Seller's update is described as "fair and balanced." It is not. On nearly every limitation point it is substantially more seller-friendly than our playbook. On several deal-specific points, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts it.

The most serious problems are structural:

- **A blanket sweep.** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims," and "limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature." Together these would quietly collapse Title, fraud and specific indemnities into the general regime.
- **No fraud carve-out.**
- **Title folded into the general cap.**

These matter more than any single number. Separately, the 20% cap happens to match our fallback, but that fallback is **not authorised**. It must not be treated as cleared.

The Disclosure Letter speaks "as at 22 September 2026." Today is 6 November 2026, so every factual matter below needs a **refreshed update**, not reliance on a six-week-old letter.

---

## Part A: Liability regime

### 1. General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft. None has been given.
- **Issue:** The Seller has opened at our fallback number. That does not clear it. A matching number is not authority. The fallback was also never meant to be conceded alongside a package that is worse on every other limitation.
- **Response:** Hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal that 20% is acceptable. If the team wants to use the fallback later, seek Amelia Frost's written approval against the specific draft.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2)
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Deductible (excess only) | Tipping (first dollar) |

- **Issue:** Both thresholds are five times ours. The deductible structure means the Buyer permanently absorbs the first AUD 250k of qualifying loss. A AUD 25k de minimis would also exclude many realistic individual claims.
- **Response:** Reject. Restate AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping basis.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months, plus the sweep
- **Playbook:** 24 months. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given.
- **Hidden override (critical):** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This reverses the default. Every Title, Tax, IP, indemnity and covenant claim would inherit the general cap, thresholds and 18-month limit unless we expressly carve each one out. That conflicts with the playbook requirement to keep the categories separate with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Response:** Restore 24 months. Delete the sweep. Draft the default the other way: general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, and each other category has its own expressly stated regime.

### 4. Fundamental / Title
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Issue:** This is a substantive concession presented as housekeeping. Title is the core of what we are buying. Capping it at 20% would mean a total title failure is compensated at AUD 4.8m against a AUD 24m price.
- **Response:** Reject. Require a separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap of AUD 24m;
  - a period of at least six years;
  - no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.

### 5. Fraud / limitations / reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out anywhere in the package.
- **Issue:** Read literally, this would try to cap and time-bar fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Fraud is a non-negotiable playbook position, and no one on the team can waive it.
- **Response:** Insert an express carve-out. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct by the Seller, its officers, employees or advisers should sit outside all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
  - caps;
  - baskets and de minimis;
  - time limits;
  - exclusive remedy;
  - non-reliance.

  Also confirm that non-reliance does not exclude claims based on the Warranties themselves.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (as at 22 September 2026), the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Issue:** This is whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure, which the playbook rejects. It would let the Seller argue that anything buried in DD-002 to DD-012, or on any public register, qualifies every warranty.
- **Response:**
  - Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Disclosure should qualify a warranty only where it is specific and fair, identifying the matter with enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope, against the warranty it qualifies.
  - The data-room index may be annexed for identification only, not as deemed disclosure.
  - Disclosure must never qualify Title, Capacity or the specific indemnities.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Issue:** This is a blanket exclusion. It covers actual, imputed and constructive ("discoverable") knowledge, and it extends to advisers. Combined with the data-room disclosure, it would gut the warranties.
- **Response:**
  - Delete cl 8.3.
  - If any qualifier survives, it should be a *Seller* knowledge qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry.
  - Buyer knowledge should never excuse Title, Capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 8. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **open**.
- **Issue:** The Seller is asserting agreement where none exists, and doing so on the general-regime terms we are rejecting above.
- **Response:** Correct the record in writing: Tax and IP are not settled. Note that we are not assuming unlimited liability either. These are to be negotiated as separate categories.

---

## Part B: Deal-specific matters

### 9. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL 2)
- **Seller Update:** the consent is "addressed." The Seller will use reasonable endeavours, and the condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter:** **no** final written consent and **no** evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.
- **Issue:** The Update's "addressed" is contradicted by the Seller's own letter. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. Under the consent-on-delivery mechanic, a consent letter whose 11.3 conditions remain unmet would still satisfy the CP. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this materiality.
- **Response:** Make it a Completion condition that requires:
  - effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent under cl 11.2; and
  - documentary evidence before Completion that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied.

  Strengthen the Seller's obligation beyond reasonable endeavours, and preserve the Buyer's right not to waive. Request a current status update, given the 22 September date.

### 10. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL 3)
- **Seller:** a release is "to be provided following Completion." About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and the letter confirms it is neither repaid nor discharged.
- **Issue:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company whose assets remain encumbered, and possibly triggers change-control 8.1 at Completion.
- **Response:** Require all of the following:
  - a **current** payout letter from Riverlark;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds in the funds flow;
  - executed security releases and discharge (cl 9.2) delivered at Completion.

  A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable Riverlark undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which we have. Treat the AUD 3.2m as approximate until a current payout figure is obtained.

### 11. Employee bonuses: funds flow (DL 5)
- **Seller:** the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics," yet the AUD 420k of DD-005 bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Issue:** This is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. Saying the bonuses are a matter for the Seller is meaningless unless the funds flow or price mechanics actually make the Seller bear them. Otherwise they are paid out of the Company post-Completion at our cost. The letter also concedes that payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed. "Agreed" is the Seller's characterisation, not ours.
- **Response:** Require one of two treatments:
  - a specific funds-flow line item for the AUD 420k **plus** all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding), paid through payroll at Completion; or
  - treatment as a Debt-like item or seller-funded deduction.

  Back either option with an indemnity. Ask for the on-cost calculation.

### 12. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)
- **Seller:** the existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate."
- **Issue:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room. The risk is wider than one payment: it covers ownership of, and the right to use, the Project Materials. DD-010's AUD 180k open figure is unverified in **both** directions, so we should not assume it is owed or that it has been paid.
- **Response:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or be entitled to use the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims. Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of the outstanding fees plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a Completion deliverable. Request bank evidence of the payment status.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL 6)
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Issue:** That is an assertion, and the facts do not support it either way. About 1,240 records may have been exposed. Access, scope and any notification obligation are all unresolved. We should not accept "not material." Equally, we should not argue that there is a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or any quantified loss.
- **Response:** Seek covenants to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete the investigation;
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and consultation rights before any notification decision;
  - make no admissions or regulatory communications without Buyer input.

  Seek a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, without attaching a number. Exclude it from the disclosure-qualification and knowledge bars. Request an update, since the facts are stated as at 22 September.

### 14. Sandbar renewals (DL 8)
- **Seller:** the renewals are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Issue:** The letter itself says it does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. The Update's characterisation is therefore unsupported.
- **Response:** Neither accept "ordinary course" nor treat the AUD 330k as Debt or a price deduction. Diligence DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing, termination rights, accrual and scope, then decide treatment based on what we find. Reserve our position in the mark-up.

### 15. Title evidence (DL 10)
- **Seller:** title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
- **Issue:** The DD-012 register is an internal, Seller-supplied record, not independent proof. The letter itself concedes that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Response:** Require independent evidence of:
  - title and ownership: ASIC company extract, issue and transfer history, constitution;
  - absence of encumbrances: PPSR searches against the Seller and Company;
  - authority: Seller board approvals and executed share transfer.

  Keep Title warranties in the fundamental regime (see item 4).

### 16. Office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)
- The letter says the lease has a notification obligation only, and that Mossvale's restriction is not triggered by a share sale. These are reasonable on their face but are the Seller's reading.
- **Response:** Have our team review DD-007 and DD-009 for change-of-control language. At minimum, make lease notification a Completion or post-Completion deliverable. Do not let DL 1.4 non-admissions limit our own assessment of what is legally required.

---

## Part C: Process points

- **Authority.** No fallback, including the 20% cap and the 18-month period, has been approved by Amelia Frost. Do not concede either. Any move needs her written approval referencing the specific draft.
- **"Agreed / addressed / settled / adequate" language.** The Update repeatedly describes open points as agreed or resolved (funds flow, Bluefen, Ironquay, Tax/IP). Correct each one in writing so the record does not drift.
- **Internal inconsistency.** Use the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (items 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 10) to rebut the Update. The Update's characterisations cannot be reconciled with the letter's factual statements.
- **Stale facts.** Request a refreshed disclosure update and a bring-down of all matters as at a current date. Distinguish verified updates from Seller assertions.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **Hold 25% / AUD 6.0m**; fallback not authorised |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping (first dollar)** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | **24 months**; fallback not authorised |
| 3 | Sweep clause | All limitations apply to all Claims | **Delete**; reverse the default |
| 4 | Title / Capacity | Same as general | **100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket and knowledge bar** |
| 5 | Fraud | No carve-out; limits apply to all Claims | **Full carve-out**; non-negotiable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room and public registers | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete**; at most named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry |
| 8 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **Open**; separate categories |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | **Effective consent plus evidence of cl 11.3 conditions as CP** |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | **Current payout, direct repayment, releases at Completion** |
| 11 | Bonuses | Not in funds flow | **Line item or seller-funded: AUD 420k plus on-costs** |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity | **Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure; verify AUD 180k** |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preservation, investigation and update covenants; specific indemnity; no assumptions either way** |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Diligence first; no automatic Debt or price treatment** |
| 15 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | **Independent ASIC, PPSR and authority evidence** |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | **Verify independently** |

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Fraud carve-out, deletion of the sweep clause, and the Title regime.
2. Disclosure and buyer-knowledge provisions.
3. Bluefen, Riverlark and bonuses.
4. Cap, thresholds and period.
5. Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar and title evidence.
=== END ADVICE ===
